summary: Russia launched a massive drone offensive on 28 November, firing jet-powered Shahed/Geran UAVs from Orel, Millerovo, and Donetsk against Kyiv, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, Dnipropetrovsk, and other regions, killing at least 7 in Nizhyn and damaging critical infrastructure in Kyiv and Bila Tserkva. Ukrainian air defenses engaged numerous drones over the capital, with impacts reported in Desnyansky, Svyatoshyn, and Troyeshchyna districts. Concurrently, Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge with a "significant" number of Neptune missiles, while Germany pledged €11.6 billion in 2027 military aid including air defense systems and drone interceptor funding.
key_points: Russia launched a massive wave of jet-powered Shahed/Geran drones from Orel, Millerovo, and Donetsk directions targeting multiple Ukrainian regions including Kyiv, Chernihiv, and Zhytomyr. (Source: @eRadarrua/133534)
At least 7 people were killed and 7 injured in Nizhyn, Chernihiv region, from a Russian strike on an enterprise on 27 November, with rescue operations completed. (Source: @eRadarrua/133540)
A Russian drone strike hit critical infrastructure in Kyiv, causing potential power and water supply disruptions, per Mayor Klitschko. (Source: @UkraineNow/85612)
Bila Tserkva suffered a Geran-5 strike on a thermal power plant/warehouse, injuring three, damaging a garage cooperative and apartment windows. (Source: @UkraineNow/85608)

Ukrainian forces conducted a significant Neptune missile strike on the Crimean Bridge, with the Navy launching a "significant" number of missiles and other units striking for hours. (Source: @UkraineNow/85606)

Germany's 2027 federal budget allocates €11.6 billion for military aid to Ukraine, maintaining near-current levels, including IRIS-T, Patriot, and drone interceptor funding. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24035)
Russian tactical aviation activity increased on the eastern front, posing a threat of aviation weapon use in frontline areas. (Source: @kpszsu/99985)
Russian drones attacked the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov region and the Samara oil pipeline station, causing a large fire at the refinery. (Source: @eRadarrua/133532)

sections.executive_summary: Russia conducted a large-scale drone offensive on 28 November, launching jet-powered Shahed/Geran UAVs from Orel, Millerovo, and Donetsk against Kyiv, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, Dnipropetrovsk, and other regions, killing at least 7 in Nizhyn and damaging critical infrastructure in Kyiv and Bila Tserkva. Ukrainian air defenses engaged numerous drones over the capital, with impacts reported in Desnyansky, Svyatoshyn, and Troyeshchyna districts. Concurrently, Ukraine struck the Crimean Bridge with a "significant" number of Neptune missiles, while Germany pledged €11.6 billion in 2027 military aid including air defense systems and drone interceptor funding.

points: Ukrainian air defenses engaged multiple Russian drones over Kyiv on 28 November: a Geran-5 flew over Irpin toward Kyiv at 100m altitude targeting Akademmistechko, Svyatoshyn, and Berkovets districts; a jet-powered Shahed attacked Troyeshchyna and TEC-6; another Geran-5 struck the Desnyansky district; two jet Shaheds targeted Khmelnytskyi city; and a Geran-5 entered Kyiv from Obolon toward Podil and Left Bank neighborhoods. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78809, @mon1tor_ua/78820, @mon1tor_ua/78822, @mon1tor_ua/78812, @mon1tor_ua/78807)

Ukraine's Navy executed a major strike on the Crimean Bridge using a "significant" number of Neptune anti-ship missiles; the launching brigade immediately relocated to avoid Russian counterstrikes, while other Ukrainian units continued striking the bridge for several hours. (Source: @UkraineNow/85606)

Ukraine facilitated the return of 9 children from Russian-occupied territories (Kherson, Zaporizhzhia, Crimea), bringing the total number of repatriated children to 2,875; the group included a grandmother accompanying a grandson and a graduate of the Oleshky orphanage requiring special support. (Source: @UkraineNow/85585)

Ukraine transmitted Black Sea ceasefire conditions to international partners to ensure safe navigation and agricultural exports; Kyiv awaits Russia's response, which has added demands including oil exports, while Ukraine insists any energy ceasefire must cover all energy infrastructure components. (Source: @UkraineNow/85595)

The Defense Procurement Agency is preparing a supplier blacklist to temporarily block companies from defense tenders; military units have ordered over 100 billion UAH of equipment via the DOT-Chain system with an average 8-day delivery timeline; manufacturers bear quality responsibility for FPV drones, while NATO standards apply to new and partner-supplied equipment. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24033)

Ukrainian military intelligence (HUR) is fundraising for optical-fiber FPV drones immune to electronic warfare, costing 25,000 UAH each, to strike enemy logistics, personnel, and ammunition depots; the campaign aims to close within one week. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78805)

Russia launched a coordinated drone wave on 28 November from three primary sites: Orel (3 groups of jet UAVs), Millerovo (2 groups), and Donetsk (2 groups), targeting Kyiv, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, Dnipropetrovsk, and other regions throughout the day. (Source: @eRadarrua/133534)

A Russian strike on an industrial enterprise in Nizhyn, Chernihiv region, on 27 November killed 7 civilians and injured 7; State Emergency Service completed rescue operations on 28 November, recovering one survivor from the rubble. (Source: @eRadarrua/133540)

A Geran-5 drone struck a thermal power plant/warehouse in Bila Tserkva, Kyiv region, injuring three people, igniting a fire in a garage cooperative, and shattering windows in two apartment buildings from the blast wave. (Source: @UkraineNow/85608, @mon1tor_ua/78815)
Russian drones hit critical infrastructure in Kyiv, prompting Mayor Klitschko to warn of potential electricity and water supply disruptions across the capital. (Source: @UkraineNow/85612)

Russian tactical aviation showed increased activity on the eastern front, creating a threat of guided bomb and missile strikes against Ukrainian frontline positions in Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia directions. (Source: @kpszsu/99985)

Russian drones attacked the Novoshakhtinsk oil refinery in Rostov region and the Samara linear production dispatch station (a major Urals blend hub) overnight 28 November, causing a large-scale fire at the refinery; damage assessments are ongoing. (Source: @eRadarrua/133532)

Russian citizens massed at Estonian border crossings attempting to enter before Estonia's 1 December closure of all border points with Russia, leading to pushing and fights at checkpoints. (Source: @UkraineNow/85613)

Russian forces advanced near Mala Tokmachka in Zaporizhzhia region, according to the latest DeepState map update, indicating continued pressure on Ukrainian defensive lines in the Orikhiv sector. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24034)

Russian tactical aviation operates actively along the eastern front, posing an imminent threat of aviation-guided weapons use against Ukrainian positions in frontline areas of Donetsk and Zaporizhzhia oblasts. (Source: @kpszsu/99985)

Russian drone launch sites at Millerovo and Donetsk (2 groups each) directly support eastern front operations, with jet-powered Shaheds likely targeting rear logistics and air defense positions in Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. (Source: @eRadarrua/133534)

Multiple jet-powered UAVs transited Chernihiv region on 28 November: one passed Kulikivka and Bakhmach heading south; another flew past Kozelets toward Kyiv region; a third passed Snovsk southward; a fourth flew past Koriukivka toward Mena; and a fifth headed toward Nizhyn from the north. (Source: @kpszsu/99969, @kpszsu/99991, @kpszsu/99987, @kpszsu/100001, @kpszsu/99990)
A new jet UAV launched from Russia's Bryansk region entered northern Chernihiv region, while another passed Slavutych on the Chernihiv-Kyiv boundary. (Source: @eRadarrua/133514, @eRadarrua/133515)

Kyiv region air defenses tracked UAVs approaching Ivankiv and Bila Tserkva; Zhytomyr region reported a jet UAV north of Ovruch and two maneuvering in Dnipro suburbs (Karnaukhivka, Vasylivka); a jet UAV from Mykolaiv region flew toward Bobrynets in Kirovohrad region. (Source: @eRadarrua/133526, @eRadarrua/133503)

Russian reconnaissance drones actively operated across Chernihiv, Kyiv, and Zhytomyr regions throughout 28 November, indicating persistent ISR efforts along the northern approaches to Kyiv. (Source: @eRadarrua/133503)

Three jet-powered UAVs launched from occupied Crimea targeted Odesa region, with one passing near Karnaliivka; another flew past Buialyk toward Krasnosilka; a third approached Budynka from the northwest. (Source: @eRadarrua/133552, @kpszsu/99995, @kpszsu/99996)

A jet UAV entered Mykolaiv region from the Black Sea waters heading south, while another passed Ochakiv moving northwest; a jet Shahed from Mykolaiv region flew toward Haisyn district in Vinnytsia region. (Source: @kpszsu/100000, @kpszsu/99992, @mon1tor_ua/78804)

Russian drone activity from Crimea and the Black Sea demonstrates continued use of southern launch vectors to strike deep into Ukrainian territory, bypassing northern air defense concentrations. (Source: @eRadarrua/133552, @kpszsu/100000)

Kyiv experienced six air raid alerts on 28 November (08:59, 11:58, 12:03, 13:52, 14:33, 14:39) with corresponding all-clears, reflecting sustained drone threat over the capital throughout the day. (Source: @eRadarrua/133531, @eRadarrua/133535, @eRadarrua/133538, @eRadarrua/133548, @eRadarrua/133549, @eRadarrua/133550)

Russian drone launch sites identified: Orel (3 groups), Millerovo (2 groups), Donetsk (2 groups) — all launching jet-powered Shahed/Geran variants; additional launches from Bryansk region, Crimea, and Black Sea waters. (Source: @eRadarrua/133534, @eRadarrua/133514, @eRadarrua/133552, @kpszsu/100000)

Drone types observed: Geran-5 (multiple), Geran-K5-5 (Kremenchuk), jet-powered Shahed variants (Chernihiv, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Vinnytsia, Odesa, Mykolaiv); one Geran-5 flew at 100m altitude over Irpin. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78804, @mon1tor_ua/78809, @kpszsu/99969, @mon1tor_ua/78812)

Ukrainian Neptune anti-ship missiles struck the Crimean Bridge in a coordinated operation; Navy brigade launched a "significant" quantity and displaced to avoid counterstrikes, while other units continued strikes for hours. (Source: @UkraineNow/85606)

Germany's 2027 budget includes €11.6 billion for Ukrainian military aid, specifically funding IRIS-T and Patriot systems, PAC-3 missiles, Gepard maintenance, and €20 million for drone interceptor development against jet-powered Shaheds. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24035)
Poland refuses to intercept Russian missiles in its airspace due to uncontrolled debris risks, but considers intercepting over Ukrainian territory pending NATO consensus. (Source: @UkraineNow/85594)

key_developments: Russian jet-powered Shahed/Geran drones launched from Orel (3 groups), Millerovo (2 groups), and Donetsk (2 groups) targeted Kyiv, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, Dnipropetrovsk, and other regions throughout 28 November.
